title: "How Is AI Changing Jobs? Data Cleaning and Exploration"
author: "Adem Khelifi and Sam"

output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 1. Load the data

```{r}
data <- read.csv("ai_job_impact.csv", check.names = FALSE)
dim(data)      # rows and columns
names(data)    # column names
head(data)
```

## 2. Check the data

```{r}
str(data)                          # type of each column
colSums(is.na(data))               # missing values
sum(duplicated(data))              # duplicate rows
sum(duplicated(data$Employee_ID))  # duplicate IDs
```

Check the labels in the main categories:

```{r}
table(data$Industry)
table(data$AI_Adoption_Level)
table(data$Job_Status)
```

Check that the numbers are in sensible ranges:

```{r}
summary(data$Age)
summary(data$Salary_Before_AI)
summary(data$Salary_After_AI)
summary(data$Job_Satisfaction)
```

## 3. Clean the data

1. Rename the column with `%` in its name.
2. Put categories in a logical order (Low → Medium → High).
3. Add new columns: salary change in dollars and percent, whether salary went up, and age group.

```{r}
data <- data %>%
  rename(Productivity_Change_Pct = `Productivity_Change_%`) %>%
  mutate(
    AI_Adoption_Level = factor(AI_Adoption_Level, levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")),
    Automation_Risk   = factor(Automation_Risk,   levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")),
    Job_Status        = factor(Job_Status, levels = c("Unchanged", "Modified", "Replaced")),
    Salary_Change     = Salary_After_AI - Salary_Before_AI,
    Salary_Change_Pct = round(Salary_Change / Salary_Before_AI * 100, 2),
    Salary_Went_Up    = ifelse(Salary_Change > 0, "Yes", "No"),
    Age_Group         = cut(Age, breaks = c(17, 29, 39, 49, 59),
                            labels = c("18-29", "30-39", "40-49", "50-59"))
  )

head(data)
```

## 4. Summary tables

### Overall

```{r}
data %>%
  summarise(
    employees          = n(),
    avg_salary_before  = mean(Salary_Before_AI),
    avg_salary_after   = mean(Salary_After_AI),
    avg_salary_change  = mean(Salary_Change_Pct),
    pct_salary_went_up = mean(Salary_Went_Up == "Yes") * 100
  )
```

### By AI adoption level

```{r}
data %>%
  group_by(AI_Adoption_Level) %>%
  summarise(
    employees         = n(),
    avg_salary_change = mean(Salary_Change_Pct),
    avg_productivity  = mean(Productivity_Change_Pct),
    avg_satisfaction  = mean(Job_Satisfaction)
  )
```

### By industry

```{r}
data %>%
  group_by(Industry) %>%
  summarise(
    employees         = n(),
    avg_salary_before = mean(Salary_Before_AI),
    avg_salary_change = mean(Salary_Change_Pct),
    pct_modified_or_replaced = mean(Job_Status != "Unchanged") * 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_modified_or_replaced))
```

### Job status

```{r}
data %>%
  count(Job_Status) %>%
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100)
```

### Job roles with the highest and lowest salary change

```{r}
role_summary <- data %>%
  group_by(Job_Role) %>%
  summarise(avg_salary_change = mean(Salary_Change_Pct)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_salary_change))

head(role_summary, 5)   # top 5
tail(role_summary, 5)   # bottom 5
```

## 5. Visuals

### Salary change by AI adoption level

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = AI_Adoption_Level, y = Salary_Change_Pct, fill = AI_Adoption_Level)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "AI adoption level", y = "Salary change (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Job status by industry

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Industry, fill = Job_Status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of employees", fill = "Job status") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

### Productivity change by AI adoption level

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = AI_Adoption_Level, y = Productivity_Change_Pct)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(x = "AI adoption level", y = "Productivity change (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Distribution of salary change

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Salary_Change_Pct)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2.5, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Salary change (%)", y = "Number of employees") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Salary before vs after AI

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Salary_Before_AI, y = Salary_After_AI, color = AI_Adoption_Level)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Salary before AI ($)", y = "Salary after AI ($)", color = "AI adoption") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 6. What we found

- No missing values, duplicate rows, or duplicate IDs; all labels are consistent.
- About 67% of employees earned more after AI; the average salary change was about +6%.
- Salary change rises with AI adoption: about +2.5% (Low), +4.7% (Medium), +10.4% (High).
- Productivity change is also higher with more AI: about 8% (Low) vs 11% (High).
- IT has the most jobs modified or replaced (about 51%); Manufacturing the fewest (about 38%).
- Doctors, Data Analysts, and Sales Associates had the biggest salary gains (about +8%); Supervisors the smallest (about +4%).
- Job satisfaction is about the same (about 6 out of 9) across all groups.
